The photo matches the exterior under the world’s longest single-span roof-support arch—133 metres tall and a landmark from much of north-west London. Official stadium tours take visitors behind the scenes on non-event days; the tour entrance is on Level 1 behind the Bobby Moore statue. FA Cup finals, England internationals, NFL games and major concerts still fill the bowl through 2025–2026.
facts.best_time: Clear daylight for arch and bowl exterior photos; weekday non-event mornings for quieter plazas. Check the events calendar before booking a tour—match or show prep can switch you to an Express Tour without player areas.
facts.how_to_get_there: Wembley Park / Olympic Way, HA9 0WS, London. Tube/Overground to Wembley Park (Jubilee/Metropolitan) or Wembley Central (Bakerloo/Overground); follow Olympic Way to the stadium.
facts.good_to_know: OPEN and hosting events and stadium tours through 2025–2026 (official site lists England fixtures and tours into late 2026). Restricted bag policy applies on event days; allow about two hours for a full tour.

facts.one_liner: Montjuïc’s Olympic Stadium—1992 Games host, not Camp Nou—on the Anella Olímpica esplanade.
facts.why_go: Estadi Olímpic Lluís Companys (often Estadi Olímpic de Montjuïc) crowns Barcelona’s Olympic Ring on Montjuïc; it staged the athletics and ceremonies of the 1992 Summer Olympics. The photo is an exterior panorama of this venue—not Camp Nou—showing the classic bowl and surrounding Anella Olímpica landscape with Palau Sant Jordi nearby. Visitors enter via the Old Marathon Gate under Pau Gargallo’s equestrian “Genets” sculptures and can see Ramón Bigas’s Olympic cauldron before walking through to the esplanade. FC Barcelona used the stadium as a temporary home while Camp Nou was rebuilt and returned to the renovated Camp Nou in late 2025; the Olympic Stadium itself remains open for visits and events.
facts.best_time: Summer hours (1 Apr–31 Oct) 10:00–19:00 and winter (1 Nov–31 Mar) 10:00–17:00 for the visitor area; esplanade opens earlier. Event/concert set-ups can close access for weeks—check the official visit page before you go.
facts.how_to_get_there: Passeig Olímpic 17/19, 08038 Barcelona (Anella Olímpica, Montjuïc). Metro L1/L3 to Espanya then escalators/bus up Montjuïc, or bus lines serving the Olympic Ring; taxis and rideshares drop at the esplanade.
facts.good_to_know: OPEN for public visits 2025–2026 on non-event schedules (official Estadi Olímpic site). Palau Sant Jordi interiors are not on the visit route. Do not confuse with Spotify Camp Nou in Les Corts.

Tour Bernabéu (Gate 84) covers the museum, panoramic bowl views, and usually dressing rooms and dugouts when match ops allow. It remains one of Madrid’s busiest sports landmarks through the 2025–2026 calendar.
facts.best_time: Non-match weekdays for the fullest tour route; Mondays–Saturdays 09:00–19:00 and Sundays/holidays 09:30–18:30 except 25 Dec and 1 Jan. On match days tours typically end 5½ hours before kick-off; dressing rooms/benches close the day before and on match day.

facts.good_to_know: OPEN daily for Tour Bernabéu 2025–2026 (official Real Madrid / Turismo Madrid). Route and hours can change for events—confirm on realmadrid.com before visiting. Bernabéu Market food hall is reached via Gate 54.

facts.one_liner: Milan’s Giuseppe Meazza—San Siro—red roof beams, helical towers, Museum&Tour at Gate 6.
facts.why_go: Stadio Giuseppe Meazza, universally called San Siro, is Milan’s historic football cathedral shared for decades by AC Milan and Inter. The exterior photo shows the layered rings, spiral access towers and distinctive red roof trusses that define the stadium’s silhouette. Museum&Tour (entrance beside Gate 6) walks dressing rooms, tunnel, pitchside and the San Siro Museum; a seasonal Skywalk follows the red beams high above the stands. The venue remains open for tours and matches in 2025–2026 while city and club plans for a long-term successor continue to evolve.

facts.one_liner: FC Bayern’s Fröttmaning home—Herzog & de Meuron’s illuminated ETFE cushion façade.
facts.why_go: Allianz Arena opened in 2005 in Munich-Fröttmaning as a purpose-built football stadium designed by Herzog & de Meuron. The photo focuses on the exterior detail that made it famous: diamond-shaped air-filled ETFE cushions (officially about 2,874 panels covering the roof and façade) that form a luminous membrane shell, lit in club colours after dark. FC Bayern München owns and plays here; Arena Tours explain the façade and take you through stands, tunnel and pitchside, with the FC Bayern Museum on the same visit. Night matches still turn the shell red for home fixtures through the 2025–2026 seasons.
facts.best_time: Non-match days for Museum + Arena Tour (most days except 25 Dec, 31 Dec, 1 Jan); dusk or night for the LED façade. Book tours online ahead—same-day tickets often sell out.
facts.how_to_get_there: Werner-Heisenberg-Allee 25, 80939 Munich (Fröttmaning). U-Bahn U6 to Fröttmaning, then the pedestrian esplanade to the Arena; parking is extensive but match days are congested.
facts.good_to_know: OPEN for FC Bayern Museum and Arena Tours 2025–2026 (allianz-arena.com). Museum hours typically 10:00–18:00; museum renovation windows can temporarily alter the Arena View product—check the ticket shop.

facts.one_liner: Berlin’s colonnaded Olympic Stadium—1936 Games stage, Hertha home, EURO 2024 final venue.
facts.why_go: Olympiastadion Berlin is the monumental stadium at Olympischer Platz, rebuilt for the 1936 Olympic Games and comprehensively renovated with a modern PTFE roof for the 2006 FIFA World Cup. The photo shows the exterior colonnades and massing that still dominate the Olympiapark approach. On non-event days you can walk the stands and grounds with info boards or a multimedia guide, or join guided Highlight tours; Hertha BSC plays Bundesliga here, and the stadium hosted the UEFA EURO 2024 final. Roughly 300,000 sightseeing visitors a year make it one of Berlin’s major sports landmarks.
facts.best_time: Non-event days when the visitor centre lists full opening (often ~09:00–19:00 in season); Fridays/Saturdays may be guided-tours-only in some weeks. Avoid Hertha home matches and major concerts for sightseeing access.
facts.how_to_get_there: Olympischer Platz 3, 14053 Berlin. S-Bahn Olympiastadion (S3/S9) or U-Bahn Olympia-Stadion (U2); follow signs to the visitor centre at the east side.
facts.good_to_know: OPEN for sightseeing and guided tours 2025–2026 (olympiastadion.berlin). Last entry usually 30 minutes before closing; visitor centre closes on Hertha home days and major events—confirm hours online.

facts.why_go: Estádio Jornalista Mário Filho, universally known as Maracanã, is Rio de Janeiro’s most famous football ground and a venue for the 1950 and 2014 FIFA World Cup finals plus the 2016 Olympic football tournament. The exterior photo shows the modern bowl and surrounding complex after post-2014 upgrades along Avenida Rei Pelé. The official Maracanã Tour (~50 minutes) typically includes locker rooms, mixed zone, press areas, historic memorabilia (Pelé, Garrincha, Zico) and pitch access when operations allow. Flamengo, Fluminense and Brazil national-team fixtures still pack the stands in 2025–2026.
facts.best_time: Non-match mornings for the fullest tour (site often lists ~09:00–17:00 with earlier last entry). NFL, derbies and concerts can close the tour for days—always check tourmaracana.com.br before you go.

facts.good_to_know: OPEN for matches and the official Tour Maracanã in 2025–2026, with temporary closures for special events (e.g. NFL windows). Bring ID as required for entry; confirm last-entry times on the day.

Its natural acoustics have made it a legendary venue for artists from the Beatles to U2, and by day the park’s trails and stairs are open for hiking and workouts.

facts.best_time: Spring and autumn for mild weather; tours year-round.

facts.good_to_know: Bullfighting is controversial; architecture tours are a way to visit without attending.
